obligation: FAR 52.204-21 Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
basis: The clause is in FC-1. FAR 4.1903 requires it whenever FCI may reside in or transit the contractor's information system, with no dollar threshold and no size exemption. FC-1 drawings, submittals, daily logs and pay apps are FCI and sit on the owner's SaaS accounts, laptop, phone and home network

obligation: FAR 52.204-25 Section 889 prohibition (covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment)
basis: The clause is in FC-1, with no size exemption. Paragraph (b)(2) prohibits use of covered equipment regardless of whether the use is in performance of a federal contract, so it reaches the owner's own devices; paragraph (d) sets the reporting duty. The January 2026 SAM representation (52.204-26) relies on it

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
basis: FC-1 is a VA civilian contract. The DoD subcontract is expected to carry FCI only; no CUI or covered defense information is expected or held. Analyzed for applicability only

obligation: CMMC Program (32 CFR Part 170) and DFARS 252.204-7021
basis: The prime's DoD task order includes DFARS 252.204-7021 at CMMC Level 1 (Self), and the prime requires a current Final Level 1 (Self) status with an SPRS affirmation before awarding the subcontract (32 CFR 170.23(a)(1); DFARS 252.204-7021(f)(2)). The subcontract (about $45,000) is above the $2,000 micro-purchase threshold for construction subject to the wage rate requirements (FAR 2.101)

The SAM representations, renewed in January 2026, answer whether the company uses covered telecommunications equipment or services after a reasonable inquiry (52.204-26(c)(2)). The January 2026 answer was 'does not use'
The clause is in FC-1. A covered article found during performance is reported within 3 business days (52.204-23(c))

obligation: FAR 52.232-27 prompt payment for construction and FAR 52.232-33 payment by EFT through SAM
basis: Both clauses are in FC-1: subcontractors are paid within 7 days of receiving the Government's payment (52.232-27(c)(1)), and the VA pays by EFT to the bank account in SAM (52.232-33(b)); if the SAM EFT information is wrong, the loss may fall on the company (52.232-33(e)(2))
The clause is in FC-1 and construction wage rate requirements apply: weekly certified payrolls from subcontractors and payroll records kept 3 years

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, disposal and breach notice)
basis: The statute's definition of covered entity names a sole proprietorship (501.171(1)(b)). The company holds personal information of Florida residents: W-9 forms with Social Security numbers for the 8 subcontractors who are sole proprietors, in the accounting SaaS and as email attachments, and account credentials
No CUI is held or expected; the FC-1 documents and the prime's request carry no CUI markings. The owner will refuse CUI work

obligation: FAR Part 40 clauses under an agency class deviation (FAR 52.240-91 and 52.240-93)
basis: FC-1 was awarded on 2026-03-09 with FAR 52.204-21 and 52.204-25 and keeps them until modified. A new award under a class deviation would carry FAR 52.240-93 (the same 15 requirements) and FAR 52.240-91

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company is not a health care provider, health plan or clearinghouse (45 CFR 160.103). The dental office build-out contract covers construction work only, and no patient information is exchanged
The company takes no card payments: private clients pay by ACH or check and the VA by EFT
The company is a sole proprietorship, not a public company

obligation: State AI laws on consequential decisions
basis: The AI bid assistant makes no decision about a person (employment; credit; housing; and similar). The company works only in Florida

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Applies to the AI vendor's own claims about its tool; not decomposed into requirement rows
Used as the benchmark where no FAR requirement applies (for example separation of duties and audit record protection) and for the crosswalk
